explanation: Cultural Atlas notes that close friends of the same gender in Egypt may hold hands or kiss cheeks when greeting in public, consistent with the broader pattern that touching during greetings depends heavily on how well people know each other. Between people of the opposite gender, especially on a first meeting, a handshake or verbal greeting is the safer default.
local_tip: Let a same-gender Egyptian friend initiate a cheek-kiss greeting if they choose to; with the opposite gender or someone you've just met, stick to a handshake (if they extend first) or a verbal greeting.

also_check.note: Cheek-kissing (la bise) is a standard greeting among friends and acquaintances of any gender.
Cheek-kissing is common among the same gender, but cross-gender greetings in public are strictly avoided.
Cheek-kissing isn't a traditional greeting; a bow is expected instead.
